translations.translatedText: # Radio Clear News Sunday 6.8.2023
Interest rates. Storm. Europe's weather. Rescuers to Portugal. Weather.
## Deposit interest rates

![A combined image shows the logos of OP, Nordea and Danske Bank side by side.](https://img.img-cdn.yle.fi/crop_extract,w_1919,h_1079,x_1081,y_0/crop_fill,w_767,h_431,ar_16:9,dpr_1/f_auto/39-115234764ce0abcd5a5f/1692182620)
Open image viewer
Few banks in Finland pay deposit interest on current accounts. Photo: Juho Liukkonen / Yle, Derrick Frilund / Yle, Ismo Pekkarinen / AOP
The vast majority of Finnish banks do not pay deposit interest on current accounts.
At the same time, customers themselves have to pay interest of more than 4 percent, for example on mortgages.

Professor of finance Vesa Puttonen says that banks do not pay interest on current accounts because customers do not demand it. Competition for deposit interest rates is not common here, Puttonen says.
Banks hold more than 80 billion euros in current accounts.
Among the traditional banks, only Handelsbanken and S-Pankki pay interest on current accounts. Handelsbanken pays half a percent and S-Pankki pays 0.3 percent to its customer-owners.
## The storm arrives
![Storm clouds above a suburb of Helsinki.](https://img.img-cdn.yle.fi/crop_extract,w_3024,h_1701,x_0,y_1330/crop_fill,w_767,h_431,ar_16:9,dpr_1/f_auto/39-115157364cbd07c0f6bc/1691079125)
Open image viewer
Rain clouds above a suburb of Helsinki on 3 August. Photo: Julius Niiniranta
Meteorologists warn of a strong storm.

A severe storm is expected to reach Finland, as things stand, during the night between Monday and Tuesday. It comes to Finland from the south and moves to the central parts of the country during Tuesday.

Laura Tuomola, a meteorologist at the Finnish Meteorological Institute, says that heavy rain, lightning and hail are expected. Thunder gusts may be strong, and wind gusts may be as high as 25 metres per second.
Tuomola says that under a storm it is not worth going out boating, and loose items are worth gathering from the yard and bringing indoors.
## Europe's weather
![A person wades through flood water.](https://img.img-cdn.yle.fi/crop_extract,w_5120,h_2880,x_0,y_0/crop_fill,w_767,h_431,ar_16:9,dpr_1/f_auto/39-115271864cf848993725/1691321557)
Open image viewer
Heavy rain in Austria has caused floods and mudslides. Photo: Gerd Eggenberger / AFP
Extreme weather also continues elsewhere in Europe. There are forest fires in Southern Europe, and heavy rain and floods in Central Europe.

In Slovenia the floods have caused major damage. At least 4 people have died. In addition, flood water has covered large areas, and the economic damage is expected to reach at least half a billion euros.
The storms have also caused floods in Austria and Hungary, and strong hailstorms in Germany.
## Rescuers to Portugal
![Rescue workers putting out a forest fire.](https://img.img-cdn.yle.fi/crop_extract,w_1536,h_864,x_0,y_698/crop_fill,w_767,h_431,ar_16:9,dpr_1/f_auto/39-115256364cf2c6c3e4a8/1691299052)
Open image viewer
Finnish rescuers helped put out forest fires in Greece last year. Photo: Sami Meriläinen / Emergency Services College
Finland is sending rescuers to Portugal to help put out forest fires.
About 50 rescuers are leaving Finland for Portugal in two different groups. Both groups will be in Portugal for two weeks.
The forest fire season in Southern Europe usually lasts from June to September. Portugal is one of the countries in Europe that suffer most from forest fires.
## Monday's weather
![Monday's weather map](https://img.img-cdn.yle.fi/crop_extract,w_1919,h_1080,x_0,y_0/crop_fill,w_767,h_431,ar_16:9,dpr_1/f_auto/39-115278464cfaacc453ff/1691331318)
Open image viewer
Photo: Yle
Tomorrow during the day, in a large part of the country, it will be dry and sunny. In Northern Finland there will be rain and thunderstorm showers. The temperature is between 20 and 32 degrees.
